question: A man with AF has a CHA2DS2-VASc score of 3. Which recommendation applies?

options.A: Anticoagulation is recommended (Class 1) because estimated risk is in the at least 2% per year range
options.C: Aspirin alone is the Class 1 therapy
options.D: No therapy until a score of 6
options.E: Anticoagulation only if he is in persistent AF

correctAnswerText: Anticoagulation is recommended (Class 1) because estimated risk is in the at least 2% per year range
explanation: Class 1, level A: anticoagulation is recommended when annual thromboembolic risk is at least 2%, exemplified by CHA2DS2-VASc of at least 2 in men and at least 3 in women [1].
sourceArticle: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation

question: A woman with AF has a CHA2DS2-VASc score of 2. How does the guideline classify anticoagulation?

options.B: Class 2a, reasonable, because this maps to at least 1% but under 2% per year

correctAnswerText: Class 2a, reasonable, because this maps to at least 1% but under 2% per year
explanation: A score of 2 in women is the example given for annual risk of at least 1% but under 2%, where anticoagulation is reasonable (Class 2a, level A). The Class 1 threshold for women is 3 or higher [1].
sourceArticle: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation

question: What annual risk threshold does the guideline use for a Class 1 anticoagulation recommendation?
explanation: Anticoagulation is recommended when estimated annual thromboembolic risk is at least 2% per year [1].
sourceArticle: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation

question: Which pair matches the Class 1 CHA2DS2-VASc example?

options.A: At least 2 in men and at least 3 in women
options.C: At least 0 in men and 1 in women
options.D: At least 4 in men and 2 in women

correctAnswerText: At least 2 in men and at least 3 in women
explanation: The Class 1 example is CHA2DS2-VASc of at least 2 in men and at least 3 in women [1].
sourceArticle: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation

question: Why is a consensus paper on AF burden not the source used here?

options.A: Stroke-prevention thresholds are stated in the 2023 AF guideline
options.B: AF burden papers are randomised trials of anticoagulation
options.C: The guideline has no stroke section

correctAnswerText: Stroke-prevention thresholds are stated in the 2023 AF guideline
explanation: The 2023 guideline gives the Class 1 and Class 2a anticoagulation recommendations tied to annual risk and CHA2DS2-VASc. A burden consensus does not set those thresholds [1].
sourceArticle: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation
